claim: A stopped Transfer Family server is still billed: stopping it in the console, with the stop-server CLI command or the StopServer API does not change billing, which runs hourly from creation of the endpoint until you delete it.
question: I have stopped my server. Will I be billed while it is stopped?

values.display: does not impact billing

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family servers
qualifiers.condition: billing ends only when the server endpoint is deleted

evidence.quote: Yes. Stopping the server, by using the console, or by running the “stop-server” CLI command or the “StopServer” API command, does not impact billing. You are billed on an hourly basis from the time you create your server endpoint and configure access to it over one or more protocols until the time you delete it.

claim: Transfer Family bills hourly for each protocol enabled, from the time you create and configure the server endpoint until you delete it.
question: How am I billed for use of the service?

values.display: billed on an hourly basis for each of the protocols enabled

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family server endpoints

evidence.quote: You are billed on an hourly basis for each of the protocols enabled, from the time you create and configure your server endpoint, until the time you delete it.

claim: Transfer Family also bills for the amount of data uploaded and downloaded over SFTP, FTPS or FTP servers, the number of messages exchanged over AS2, and the amount of data processed by the Decrypt workflow step.
question: What else am I billed for besides the hourly protocol charge?

values.display: amount of data uploaded and downloaded

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family servers

evidence.quote: You are also billed based on the amount of data uploaded and downloaded over your SFTP, FTPS, or FTP servers, number of messages exchanged over AS2, and the amount of data processed using Decrypt workflow step.

claim: Billing does not differ whether one server endpoint enables several protocols or you use a separate endpoint for each protocol: you pay hourly for each enabled protocol and for the data transferred through each protocol.
question: Will my billing be different if I use the same server endpoint for multiple protocols or use different endpoints for each protocol?

values.display: regardless of whether same endpoint is enabled for multiple protocols

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family servers

evidence.quote: No. You are billed on an hourly basis for each of the protocols you have enabled and for the amount of data transferred through each of the protocols, regardless of whether same endpoint is enabled for multiple protocols or you are using different endpoints for each of the protocols.

claim: With SFTP connectors you are billed for the amount of data transferred and the number of connector calls.
question: Am I billed hourly for using SFTP connectors?

values.display: the amount of data transferred and the number of connector calls

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family SFTP connectors

evidence.quote: When using SFTP connectors, you are billed for the amount of data transferred and the number of connector calls.

claim: With Transfer Family web apps you only pay for your web app units.
question: How am I billed for Transfer Family web apps?

values.display: web app units

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family web apps

evidence.quote: With Transfer Family web apps, you only pay for your web app units.

claim: Transfer Family supports three identity provider options for servers: Service Managed, Microsoft Active Directory, and Custom Identity Providers.
question: What identity provider options are supported by the service?

values.display: three identity provider options

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family server endpoints

evidence.quote: The service supports three identity provider options: Service Managed, where you store user identities within the service, Microsoft Active Directory, and, Custom Identity Providers, which enable you to integrate an identity provider of your choice.

claim: Service Managed authentication is supported for server endpoints that are enabled for SFTP only.
question: Which protocols can use Service Managed authentication?

values.display: enabled for SFTP only

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family Service Managed authentication

evidence.quote: Service Managed authentication is supported for server endpoints that are enabled for SFTP only.

note: Check against the user guide service-managed-users and tf-server-endpoint pages before teaching; this FAQ sentence may be older than the guide.

claim: Anonymous users are currently not supported for any of the Transfer Family protocols.
question: Are anonymous users supported?

values.display: Anonymous users are currently not supported

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family, all protocols

evidence.quote: No. Anonymous users are currently not supported for any of the protocols.

claim: Storing passwords within the Transfer Family service for authentication is currently not supported.
question: Can I use service managed option for password authentication?

values.display: Storing passwords within the service for authentication is currently not supported

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family Service Managed authentication

evidence.quote: No. Storing passwords within the service for authentication is currently not supported.

claim: To integrate your own identity provider with a Transfer Family server you can use an AWS Lambda function or an Amazon API Gateway endpoint; use API Gateway if you need a RESTful API to the identity provider or want AWS WAF geo-blocking and rate limiting.
question: What options do I have to integrate my identity provider with an AWS Transfer Family server?

values.display: an AWS Lambda function, or an Amazon API Gateway endpoint

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family custom identity provider

evidence.quote: To integrate your identity provider with an AWS Transfer Family server, you can use an AWS Lambda function, or an Amazon API Gateway endpoint. Use Amazon API Gateway if you need a RESTful API to connect to an identity provider or want to leverage AWS WAF for its geo-blocking and rate limiting capabilities.

claim: Transfer Family supports setting access with Active Directory only by AD groups, not for individual AD users.
question: Can I provide access to individual AD users or to all users in a directory?

values.display: We only support setting access by AD Groups

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family with Microsoft Active Directory

evidence.quote: No. We only support setting access by AD Groups.

claim: Transfer Family support for Microsoft AD can be used only for password-based authentication; to use a mix of authentication modes, use the Custom authorizer option.
question: Can I use AD to authenticate users using SSH keys?

values.display: can only be used for password-based authentication

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family with Microsoft Active Directory

evidence.quote: No. AWS Transfer Family support for Microsoft AD can only be used for password-based authentication. To use a mix of authentication modes, use the Custom authorizer option.

claim: You can upload up to 10 SSH keys per SFTP user with Service Managed authentication; RSA, ED25519 and ECDSA keys are supported.
question: How many SSH keys can I upload per SFTP user? Which key types are supported?

values.display: up to 10 SSH keys per user

qualifiers.scope: per SFTP user, Service Managed authentication

evidence.quote: You can upload up to 10 SSH keys per user. RSA, ED25519, and ECDSA keys are supported.

claim: A VPC hosted endpoint can be restricted so that only clients in the same VPC, other VPCs you specify, or on-premises environments connected through Direct Connect, VPN or VPC peering can reach it.
question: Can I set up my server to be accessible to resources only within my VPC?

values.display: accessible only to clients within the same VPC

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family VPC hosted endpoint

evidence.quote: By using a VPC hosted endpoint for your server, you can restrict it to be accessible only to clients within the same VPC, other VPCs you specify, or in on-premises environments using networking technologies that extend your VPC such as AWS Direct Connect, AWS VPN, or VPC peering.

claim: You can use AWS Global Accelerator with a Transfer Family server endpoint to improve file transfer throughput and round-trip time for remotely located end users.
question: How do I improve performance of file transfers for remotely located end users?

values.display: AWS Global Accelerator

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family server endpoint

evidence.quote: You can use AWS Global Accelerator with your Transfer server endpoint to improve file transfer throughput and round-trip time.

claim: You do not need AWS PrivateLink for data transfer from a Transfer Family server to Amazon S3; the service does not require PrivateLink endpoints for S3 to keep traffic off the internet and cannot use them, assuming the storage service and the server are in the same Region.
question: How do AWS Transfer Family servers communicate with Amazon S3?

values.display: you do not need to use AWS PrivateLink

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family server to Amazon S3
qualifiers.condition: storage service and Transfer Family server in the same Region

evidence.quote: Because of this, you do not need to use AWS PrivateLink for data transfered from the AWS Transfer Family server to Amazon S3. The Transfer Family service doesn’t require AWS PrivateLink endpoints for Amazon S3 to keep traffic from going over the internet, and therefore cannot use those to communicate with storage services. This all assumes that the AWS storage service and the Transfer Family server are in the same region.

note: The preceding FAQ sentence says the traffic runs over internal AWS networks and does not traverse the public internet.

claim: The buckets a Transfer Family user can access are set by the IAM role and the optional scope-down policy, but you can use only a single bucket as the home directory of the user.
question: Can I provide my end users access to more than one Amazon S3 bucket?

values.display: only use a single bucket as the home directory

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family users, Amazon S3

evidence.quote: The bucket(s) your user can access is determined by the AWS IAM Role, and the optional scope-down policy you assign for that user. You can only use a single bucket as the home directory for the user.

claim: Directory rename operations, append operations, changing ownerships, permissions and timestamps, and symbolic and hard links are currently not supported over SFTP, FTPS and FTP.
question: What file operations are supported for my SFTP/FTPS/FTP users? What operations are not supported?

values.display: Directory rename operations, append operations

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family SFTP, FTPS and FTP users on Amazon S3
qualifiers.condition: answer given in the Amazon S3 access section

evidence.quote: Directory rename operations, append operations, changing ownerships, permissions and timestamps, and use of symbolic and hard links are currently not supported.

claim: Either SFTP or FTPS should be used for secure transfers over public networks.
question: Which protocols should I use for securing data while in-transit over a public network?

values.display: Either SFTP or FTPS

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family, public networks

evidence.quote: Either SFTP or FTPS should be used for secure transfers over public networks.

claim: Managed workflows can be triggered only for files uploaded over SFTP, FTPS and FTP server endpoints and process one file per execution; they are not supported for AS2 messages, for downloads, or for files transferred with SFTP connectors.
question: Which Transfer Family actions are not supported by Managed Workflows?

values.display: process one file per execution

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family managed workflows

evidence.quote: Currently, managed workflows can only be triggered for files uploaded over your SFTP, FTPS and FTP server endpoints and process one file per execution. Managed Workflows are not supported for messages exchanged over AS2, for file downloads over your server endpoints and for files transferred using SFTP connectors.

claim: You can use Transfer Family to access EFS file systems in the same AWS Region only.
question: Can I use AWS Transfer Family to access an EFS file system in a different AWS Region?

values.display: in the same AWS Region only

qualifiers.scope: AWS Transfer Family with Amazon EFS

evidence.quote: No. You can use AWS Transfer Family to access EFS file systems in the same AWS Region only.
